models.purpose: Build an undirected signed graph of the 17 goals and score each goal by six centralities.
models.summary: Each series becomes a 16-year vector. Spearman correlation on the rank vectors gives the edge evidence; edges are counted as positive, negative or neutral at a 0.6 threshold and dropped when fewer than ten series connect the two goals. The signed weight is the positive share minus the negative share. Betweenness, closeness and eigenvector centrality are then computed separately on the positive edges and on the negative edges.

models.purpose: Allocate a fixed yearly resource to goals in priority order, carry synergy and trade-off forward one year, and keep finished goals at the top.
models.summary: Completion percentages evolve for ten years. The highest-priority unfinished goal is served first; the resource left after it flows to the next, and so on. A correlation term spreads part of each goal's gain to the goals linked with it, scaled by a constant set to 5. A finished goal moves to a complete queue that outranks every unfinished goal, and returns to the top of the active list if it slips back. For the shock, the allocation is scaled by a threat coefficient and the priority vector gains a seventh entry.
